title: Smoothness of time functions and the metric splitting of globally hyperbolic spacetimes
relevance: Supplies the smooth Cauchy temporal function and smooth spacelike Cauchy levels used to construct the source slice and force target causal curves to enter the open past set.
limits: Selective full-text audit of Theorem 1.1 and its stated globally hyperbolic splitting; not an audit of every proof detail. Provides the temporal-function result only, not the bowtie lemma or any Einstein evolution uniqueness theorem.

locators.application: Cauchy temporal function has Cauchy levels; shift its value at the marked event to zero

assumptions: Smooth globally hyperbolic spacetime in the paper's Lorentzian convention.
conclusion: Every globally hyperbolic spacetime admits a smooth splitting with spacelike Cauchy levels and a temporal time coordinate.
dependencies: Earlier smooth Cauchy hypersurface and Geroch splitting results, as cited by the authors.

title: Problème de Cauchy global en relativité générale
version: Séminaire Jean Leray no. 2 (1969–1970), pp. 1–7; original French note
kind: primary research exposition of geometric uniqueness theorem
relevance: Audited for the exact scope of global Cauchy uniqueness invoked after the geometric lemma, and for whether its statement covers coupled matter.
limits: The note states and proves the global maximal-development uniqueness theorem for vacuum Einstein equations. Its introduction says the method applies to Einstein equations coupled to hyperbolic material evolution when the corresponding local existence and uniqueness theorems hold, but the body specializes to vacuum. It is not a stand-alone uniqueness proof for a particular Einstein–scalar regularity category.

locators.coupled-scope: Introduction, pp. 1–2: method depends on local existence and uniqueness and extends to hyperbolic matter systems under that premise
locators.vacuum-cauchy-data: §1, pp. 2–3: intrinsic vacuum data include induced metric and second fundamental form

assumptions: Vacuum Einstein Cauchy developments with the differentiability and global-hyperbolicity definitions in the note; the coupled-matter extension is conditional on local well-posedness/uniqueness for that matter system.
conclusion: Every admissible vacuum initial datum has a unique maximal globally hyperbolic development up to the stated data-preserving geometric isometry; the same gluing strategy applies to suitable hyperbolic matter systems once their local theory is established.
proof_status: Vacuum theorem proved in the note; coupled applications not independently proved there.
dependencies: Local geometric Cauchy existence and uniqueness; the note constructs a maximal development by the union/gluing argument.
open_questions: Which exact coupled Einstein–scalar local and global Cauchy uniqueness theorem covers the LOY quotient/axis regularity category?
Does the chosen coupling provide the field and normal-derivative data required by its uniqueness theorem from the isometry near the slice?
